name: Install a CRD and use a custom resource
objective: CKA › Cluster Architecture (extend the API). A CustomResourceDefinition teaches the apiserver a new kind; once Established, you create and manage custom resources like any built-in. Install a CRD, then create a custom resource of that new kind. This is the 'install an operator's CRDs, then drive it with CRs' skill.

questions.title: Install a CustomResourceDefinition
questions.teach:
A **CRD** registers a new API type. Key fields: `group`, `names` (kind/plural/singular), `scope` (`Namespaced`/`Cluster`), and `versions[]` each with `served`, `storage`, and an OpenAPI `schema`. Applying it makes the apiserver serve `kubectl get <plural>`.

**Gotcha:** the CRD `metadata.name` MUST be `<plural>.<group>`. After apply, the CRD needs a moment to reach `Established=True` before you can create CRs.
questions.prompt:
Install a **Namespaced** CRD for kind `Widget` in group `example.com`, version `v1`: plural `widgets`, singular `widget`, shortName `wd`, with a spec field `size` (string). The CRD's name must be `widgets.example.com`.

Target: CRD `widgets.example.com` exists and reaches condition `Established=True`.
questions.hint: `metadata.name: widgets.example.com`; `spec.group: example.com`; `spec.scope: Namespaced`; `spec.names: {kind: Widget, plural: widgets, singular: widget, shortNames: [wd]}`; one version v1 `served: true, storage: true` with `schema.openAPIV3Schema` of type object containing `spec.properties.size: {type: string}`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata: { name: widgets.example.com }
spec:
  group: example.com
  scope: Namespaced
  names: { kind: Widget, plural: widgets, singular: widget, shortNames: [wd] }
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              size: { type: string }
YAML
kubectl get crd widgets.example.com

verification.description: CRD widgets.example.com Established (Namespaced, group example.com, v1)

questions.eli5:
Kubernetes already knows a bunch of "nouns" out of the box: Pod, Service, Deployment. A **CRD** (CustomResourceDefinition) is you teaching it a brand-new noun — like adding a new word to a dictionary that everyone then understands.

Think of the API server as a **post office** that only delivers mail to address *types* it recognizes. Out of the box it knows "House," "Apartment," "PO Box." A CRD is you walking in and saying: *"From now on, 'Widget' is also a valid address type, it lives in the 'example.com' city, and here's the form people must fill out to send one."* Once the clerk writes that down and stamps it **Established**, anyone can mail a Widget and the clerk accepts it.

In the form you tell the post office:
- the **kind** (`Widget`) — the proper name
- the **plural/singular/shortName** (`widgets`/`widget`/`wd`) — nicknames so `kubectl get widgets` or `kubectl get wd` both work
- the **scope** — does a Widget live inside one room (`Namespaced`) or the whole building (`Cluster`)?
- the **schema** — which fields are allowed (here, `spec.size` must be text)

**Watch out for:**

- The CRD's **name must be exactly `<plural>.<group>`** — here `widgets.example.com`. Any other name and `kubectl apply` rejects it.
- After you apply it, there's a **short pause** before it's usable. Wait for condition **`Established=True`** — create a Widget too early and it fails.
- `Namespaced` vs `Cluster` is a **permanent choice** — picking the wrong one means deleting and recreating.
- Field names in the schema matter: if the schema says `size` is a **string**, sending a number later gets rejected.
questions.deepDive:
## Installing a CustomResourceDefinition — full rundown

### Mental model
A **CRD** extends the Kubernetes API with a **new kind**. The API server reads the CRD, then starts serving a new REST endpoint (`/apis/<group>/<version>/<plural>`) and etcd storage for it. From that moment, your custom resources behave like first-class objects: `kubectl get`, `describe`, `apply`, RBAC, labels, watches — all of it works. This is exactly how operators ship: install their CRDs, then drive them with custom resources.

### The current API: `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1`
`v1beta1` was removed in Kubernetes 1.22. Always use `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1`, which requires a **structural schema** (`schema.openAPIV3Schema`) on every served version.

### Anatomy of a CRD
```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: widgets.example.com          # MUST be <plural>.<group>
spec:
  group: example.com
  scope: Namespaced                  # or Cluster
  names:
    kind: Widget                     # CamelCase, used in CR manifests
    plural: widgets                  # lowercase, URL + `kubectl get widgets`
    singular: widget                 # lowercase
    shortNames: [wd]                 # optional, `kubectl get wd`
    listKind: WidgetList             # optional, defaults to <kind>List
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true                     # exposed over the API
    storage: true                    # exactly ONE version must be storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              size:
                type: string
```

### Field reference
| Field | Meaning | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `metadata.name` | `<plural>.<group>` | Rejected if it doesn't match exactly |
| `spec.group` | API group | Appears in CR `apiVersion` as `<group>/<version>` |
| `spec.scope` | `Namespaced` or `Cluster` | Immutable choice; changes which verbs/paths exist |
| `spec.names.kind` | CR `kind` value | CamelCase |
| `spec.names.plural` | REST path + `kubectl get` | lowercase |
| `spec.names.shortNames` | CLI aliases | optional array |
| `versions[].served` | version is reachable | can serve multiple versions |
| `versions[].storage` | persisted form in etcd | **exactly one** version true |
| `schema.openAPIV3Schema` | validation | required in `v1` (structural schema) |

### Commands
```bash
kubectl apply -f widget-crd.yaml
kubectl get crd                                  # list all CRDs
kubectl get crd widgets.example.com
kubectl describe crd widgets.example.com         # see conditions + schema

# Wait for it to be usable (great in scripts/exam):
kubectl wait --for=condition=Established crd/widgets.example.com --timeout=60s

# Inspect the Established condition directly:
kubectl get crd widgets.example.com \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Established")].status}'; echo

# Discovery — proof the API now serves it:
kubectl api-resources | grep widgets
```

### The `Established` condition
After apply, the apiextensions controller validates the CRD and sets `status.conditions`:
- **`NamesAccepted=True`** — the names don't collide with anything.
- **`Established=True`** — the new endpoint is live and ready for custom resources.

Creating a CR before `Established=True` can fail with *"no matches for kind"*. In automation, `kubectl wait --for=condition=Established` is the reliable gate.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Name mismatch** — `metadata.name` must be literally `plural.group`. The single most common CRD error.
- **No storage version / two storage versions** — exactly one `versions[]` entry must have `storage: true`.
- **Missing schema** — `v1` requires `openAPIV3Schema`; without it the apply is rejected.
- **Wrong scope** — a `Namespaced` CRD's resources need `-n`; a `Cluster` one must NOT. Scope can't be flipped on an existing CRD meaningfully.
- **Race** — don't create a CR immediately after apply; wait for `Established`.
- **`x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields`** — without it, fields not in the schema are pruned/rejected (structural schema). Add it only when you intentionally want free-form content.
- **Deleting a CRD deletes every custom resource of that kind** — cascading and irreversible.

### Quick reference
```bash
# Apply + wait, exam-safe:
kubectl apply -f widget-crd.yaml
kubectl wait --for=condition=Established crd/widgets.example.com --timeout=60s
kubectl api-resources | grep -i widget
```
Required fields checklist: `metadata.name=widgets.example.com`, `group`, `scope`, `names.{kind,plural,singular,shortNames}`, one `versions[]` with `served:true storage:true schema.openAPIV3Schema`.

questions.title: Create a custom resource
questions.teach:
Once the CRD is Established, custom resources use `apiVersion: <group>/<version>` and the CRD's `kind`. They live in a namespace (for Namespaced CRDs) and you manage them with normal `kubectl` verbs, including the shortName.

**Gotcha:** the CR's `apiVersion` is `example.com/v1` (group/version), NOT `v1`. Fields not in the CRD schema are rejected (structural schema).
questions.prompt:
In namespace `crd-learn`, create a `Widget` named `gadget` with `spec.size: large`.

Target: a Widget `gadget` exists in `crd-learn` with `spec.size == large` (visible via `kubectl -n crd-learn get wd`).
questions.hint: `apiVersion: example.com/v1`, `kind: Widget`, `metadata.name: gadget`, `spec.size: large`. Apply into namespace crd-learn.
questions.solution:
kubectl create namespace crd-learn 2>/dev/null
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: example.com/v1
kind: Widget
metadata: { name: gadget, namespace: crd-learn }
spec:
  size: large
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets

verification.description: Widget gadget exists in crd-learn with spec.size=large

questions.eli5:
In the last step you taught the cluster a new word: **Widget**. Now you actually *write a sentence using it* — you create a real Widget.

Back to the post office analogy: last time you registered "Widget" as a valid address type and handed in the blank form. Now you're filling out that form and **actually mailing a Widget** named `gadget`, writing `size: large` on it. Because Widgets live inside a specific room (`Namespaced`), you drop it into the `crd-learn` mailbox.

The one tricky bit is the **return address line** at the top — `apiVersion`. For built-in things like a Pod it's just `v1`. But for your custom Widget it has to say which *city* and *version* it belongs to: `example.com/v1` — that's `<group>/<version>`. Get that wrong and the clerk can't figure out what kind of mail this is.

Once it's in, your Widget is a normal citizen: `kubectl get widgets`, `kubectl get wd`, `describe`, `delete` — all work just like Pods.

**Watch out for:**

- **`apiVersion` is `example.com/v1`, NOT `v1`.** It's group/version, not just the version. This is the classic mistake.
- **Only fields in the schema are allowed.** The CRD said `spec.size` is a string — add a field the schema never mentioned and it gets rejected (or silently dropped).
- **It needs a namespace** because the CRD is `Namespaced`. Put it in `crd-learn`, and remember to pass `-n crd-learn` when you look for it.
- **The CRD must be `Established` first.** If step 1 isn't ready, creating the Widget fails with "no matches for kind."
- **`kind` must match exactly** — `Widget`, capital W, as declared in the CRD.
questions.deepDive:
## Creating a custom resource — full rundown

### Mental model
Once a CRD is `Established`, a **custom resource (CR)** is just an instance of the new kind — treated by the API server exactly like a built-in object. The defining difference from built-ins is the `apiVersion`: it carries your **group** (`example.com/v1`), not the bare `v1` that core objects use. The CR is validated against the CRD's OpenAPI schema and stored in etcd under the CRD's storage version.

### The CR manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: example.com/v1          # <group>/<version> — NOT just v1
kind: Widget                        # matches spec.names.kind in the CRD
metadata:
  name: gadget
  namespace: crd-learn              # required: CRD scope is Namespaced
spec:
  size: large                       # must exist in the CRD schema, type string
```
Apply it:
```bash
kubectl create namespace crd-learn   # if it doesn't exist
kubectl apply -f widget.yaml
```

### apiVersion: how group/version maps
| CRD field | CR manifest |
|---|---|
| `spec.group: example.com` | `apiVersion:` prefix → `example.com/...` |
| `versions[].name: v1` | `apiVersion:` suffix → `.../v1` |
| `spec.names.kind: Widget` | `kind: Widget` |
| `spec.scope: Namespaced` | `metadata.namespace` required |

Core/built-in objects (Pod, Service, ConfigMap) are in the **legacy core group**, which has an empty group name — that's why their `apiVersion` is just `v1`. Every CRD-backed kind always shows `group/version`.

### Managing CRs with normal kubectl verbs
```bash
kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets             # plural
kubectl -n crd-learn get wd                  # shortName
kubectl -n crd-learn get widget gadget -o yaml
kubectl -n crd-learn describe widget gadget
kubectl -n crd-learn get wd gadget \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.size}'; echo           # -> large
kubectl -n crd-learn delete widget gadget
```

### Structural schema enforcement
With `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1`, the CRD's schema is **structural** by default. Consequences:
- Fields **not declared** in the schema are **pruned** (dropped) on write — they won't persist.
- A **wrong type** (e.g. `size: 5` when schema says `string`) is **rejected** at admission.
- To intentionally allow arbitrary nested content, the CRD author must set `x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true` on that subtree.

So from a CR author's side: only fields the CRD knows about survive. If `spec.color` silently disappears, the CRD schema simply doesn't define it.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **`apiVersion: v1` instead of `example.com/v1`** → `no matches for kind "Widget"` or it's interpreted as a core object. Always use `group/version`.
- **Forgetting the namespace** on a `Namespaced` CR → it lands in `default`, and graders looking in `crd-learn` won't find it.
- **Case-sensitive `kind`** — must be exactly `Widget`.
- **CRD not Established yet** → CR creation fails; create the CRD first (and `kubectl wait --for=condition=Established`).
- **Extra/misspelled spec fields vanish** due to pruning — verify with `get -o yaml` that your value actually stored.
- **Querying without `-n`** can make you think the CR is missing when it's just in another namespace.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl create ns crd-learn 2>/dev/null
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: example.com/v1
kind: Widget
metadata: { name: gadget, namespace: crd-learn }
spec:
  size: large
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn get wd gadget -o jsonpath='{.spec.size}'; echo   # large
```
Remember: `apiVersion = <group>/<version>`, `kind` matches the CRD, namespace required for Namespaced scope, only schema-declared fields persist.
